kept_from_that_article.summary: The Information reported on July 1 that NVIDIA was providing financial guarantees to young GPU cloud providers and would repurchase unsold capacity at a pre-agreed price if they failed to find enough renters.
passages: On July 1, according to the technology news outlet The Information, NVIDIA is providing financial guarantees to young cloud service providers that lease or rent its GPUs—if these companies fail to secure enough AI developers to rent their computing capacity, NVIDIA will repurchase their unsold GPU capacity at a pre-agreed price.

kept_from_that_article.summary: Under the reported arrangements, NVIDIA will receive a share of participating cloud providers’ revenue, with the rate declining over each contract term.
passages: In return, NVIDIA will receive a percentage of these cloud providers’ revenue, with the revenue-sharing rate gradually declining over the term of the contract.

kept_from_that_article.summary: Firmus and Sharon AI have joined NVIDIA’s reported cloud-provider program, according to the report, which said three executives with existing NVIDIA business ties confirmed the arrangement.
passages: GPU cloud providers Firmus and Sharon AI have already joined the program, and three executives with existing business ties to NVIDIA confirmed the arrangement.

kept_from_that_article.summary: NVIDIA announced on July 1 a business model combining revenue sharing and credit support to help AI cloud providers procure its infrastructure without paying the full capital expenditure upfront.
passages: On July 1, NVIDIA published a statement on its official website announcing a new business model that combines revenue sharing with credit support, enabling AI cloud providers to procure NVIDIA infrastructure without bearing the full upfront capital expenditure, and allowing them to offer computing services to downstream AI-native enterprises, model developers, and corporate clients.

kept_from_that_article.summary: Sharon AI plans to deploy up to 40,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs; Firmus is constructing a Batam DSX AI Factory campus planned for up to 360 MW and 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs.
passages: Sharon AI plans to deploy up to 40,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs, while Firmus is constructing a DSX AI Factory campus in Batam, Indonesia, expected to scale up to 360 megawatts and accommodate up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs.

kept_from_that_article.summary: The Information had reported that NVIDIA was negotiating financial guarantees for OpenAI’s lease of an Ohio data center, whose full build-out could cost as much as $500 billion.
passages: According to prior reporting by The Information, NVIDIA has also recently been negotiating to provide financial guarantees for OpenAI’s lease of a large data center in Ohio—an asset that, if fully built out at current prices for chips, labor, power, and other materials, could cost as much as $500 billion.

kept_from_that_article.summary: NVIDIA’s May 2026 regulatory filing, covering the quarter ended in April, disclosed that it had added $3.5 billion in guarantees for customer data-center leases in exchange for rights to purchase their shares.
passages: According to a regulatory filing submitted by NVIDIA in May of this year (covering the quarter ended in April), NVIDIA subsequently added another $3.5 billion to guarantee customer data center leases in exchange for rights to purchase their shares.

decisive_item.title: Nvidia GPU Debt Backstop Unleashes the AI Project Trinity: Capital, Offtake and Datacenters
decisive_item.passage: Nvidia is diving even deeper, as it has started backstopping datacenter leases

meaning.what: NVIDIA backstops datacenter leases for neoclouds (a second kind of obligation)

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis says its supply-chain tracking indicates Nvidia’s second-half 2026 shipment-volume and revenue estimates are materially higher than the general market’s estimates.
passages: Nvidia revenue is skyrocketing, and even 3 years into the build out, the general market is still materially lower on shipment volumes and revenue estimates for Nvidia in the 2nd half of this year versus our through supply chain tracking in the Accelerator Model .

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis forecasts AI debt financing will exceed $7 trillion outstanding by 2029, driven by AI IT and data-center capital needs.
passages: AI Debt Financing will become a multi-trillion-dollar credit market, with over $7T of debt outstanding by 2029 driven both by AI IT Capex and AI Datacenter Capex needs for Neoclouds, datacenter builders, and even hyperscalers.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis forecasts annual AI capital expenditure, including AI IT equipment and the data centers that house it, will exceed $2 trillion in calendar 2028.
passages: Annual AI Capex – including GPUs, networking, storage and attached CPU compute as well as for the Datacenters to house AI compute – will be well north of $2T in 2028.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis forecasts cumulative AI capital expenditure from 2024 through 2029 will reach about $11.1 trillion and says credit markets will be its main funding source.
passages: Cumulative AI Capex from 2024 to 2029 will reach ~$11.1T, and credit markets will be the main funding source for this buildout.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis reports Nvidia has started providing Neoclouds take-or-pay backstops that guarantee minimum revenue on GPU capacity.
passages: This is why Nvidia has stepped in and has started backstopping GPU rental offtakes themselves . In the backstop program, Nvidia provides a take-or-pay commitment to Neoclouds – a minimum revenue guarantee on the underlying GPU capacity.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis reports Nvidia has started backstopping data-center leases as part of its Neocloud support.
passages: Here, Nvidia is diving even deeper, as it has started backstopping datacenter leases.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis says Nvidia’s backstop programme typically lasts six years and commits Nvidia to purchase compute at pre-agreed prices that vary over the term.
passages: Nvidia’s backstop program is typically six years in length, and during these six years, Nvidia stands ready to purchase compute at pre-agreed price levels that vary over the time period.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SharonAI announced a six-year Nvidia backstop for up to 40,000 GB300 GPUs at its 72MW Australian AI factory, disclosing a total backstop value of $4.88 billion and an implied average floor of about $2.33 per GPU-hour.
passages: The first is SharonAI’s 72MW AI factory in Australia. Announced in June 2026, the deal has SharonAI scaling up to as many as 40,000 GB300s under a six-year backstop. Sharon disclosed a total backstop value of $4.88B, which works out to an implied floor of about $2.33/hr/GPU on average over the six year period.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SharonAI guides that by mid-2027 its footprint will reach 132MW, including 102MW contracted, and its total Nvidia GPU count will exceed 55,000, including the 40,000 backstopped GB300s.
passages: Sharon AI’s footprint is now set to grow to 132MW with 102MW contracted, and the company guides to reaching more than 55,000 Nvidia GPUs in total (inclusive of the 40,000 GB300s backstopped) by mid-2027.

kept_from_that_article.summary: Firmus announced a 360MW Batam, Indonesia AI cluster with an Nvidia backstop on June 29, 2026; SemiAnalysis says it will likely be housed in a DayOne facility at Kabil Industrial Tech Park.
passages: Firmus’s 360MW AI Cluster in Batam, Indonesia is the next major project announced with an Nvidia backstop. It will likely be housed in a DayOne facility in Kabil Industrial Tech Park (KITP). Announced just recently on June 29 th , 2026, this project shows the scale at which Nvidia is rolling out the backstop program.

kept_from_that_article.summary: Firmus expects customer revenue of $25 billion to $30 billion over six years for its Batam project.
passages: Firmus announced that they expect $25B to $30B of customer revenue over the six years.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis says many Neoclouds are in advanced negotiations with Nvidia over backstops, while others are considering the programme.
passages: Many Neoclouds are already deep in negotiations with Nvidia, and there are still others that are considering engaging with the backstop program.
